questions.text: Agricultural Platform Financial Sustainability - SSA Context: Demonstrate long-term financial viability: (1) Revenue model (how does platform make money? sustainable beyond donor grants?); (2) Profitability timeline (when will platform be profitable?); (3) Funding sources (grants, equity, debt - diversified?); (4) Burn rate vs runway (how long can platform operate?); (5) Local entity financials (not just parent company - local operations sustainable?); (6) Currency risk management (volatile local currencies - hedging strategies?); (7) Farmer affordability (pricing sustainable for smallholders?).
questions.evidence_required: Financial statements (local entity), Revenue model documentation, Profitability projections, Funding source breakdown, Burn rate analysis, Currency hedging strategies, Farmer affordability analysis
questions.africa_specific_notes: Many agtech platforms donor-dependent - not sustainable. Local entity must be viable, not just parent company. Currency volatility major risk. Farmer affordability critical.

questions.text: Exit Risk & Farmer Data Protection: Plan for platform failure or exit: (1) What happens to farmer data if platform shuts down (data portability, deletion)?; (2) What happens to farmer credit history (can farmers take to other platforms)?; (3) What happens to farmer farm records (years of data - who owns it)?; (4) Transition plan (how are farmers migrated to alternative platforms?); (5) Refund policy (prepaid services, unused credits); (6) Communication plan (how are farmers notified of shutdown?).
questions.evidence_required: Data portability procedures, Credit history transfer mechanisms, Farm records ownership documentation, Platform exit/transition plan, Refund policies, Farmer communication protocols
questions.africa_specific_notes: High platform failure rate in Africa. Farmers lose years of data, credit history. Exit planning mandatory. Farmer data sovereignty critical.

questions.text: Local Entity Commitment & Investment: Demonstrate genuine local presence and investment: (1) Local entity registration (not just brass plate - real operations?); (2) Local staff (how many? what roles? senior positions?); (3) Local offices (physical presence in-country?); (4) Local investment (capex in local infrastructure, not just opex?); (5) Local partnerships (with cooperatives, input suppliers, buyers); (6) Profit repatriation policy (are profits reinvested locally or extracted?).
questions.evidence_required: Local entity registration documents, Local staff roster and org chart, Office lease agreements, Local investment documentation, Partnership agreements, Profit reinvestment policies
questions.africa_specific_notes: Many platforms extractive - profit to Global North, minimal local investment. Local entity must be real, not shell company. Local hiring and reinvestment critical.

questions.text: Long-Term Agricultural Market Commitment: Demonstrate sustained commitment to African agriculture: (1) Years of operation in Sub-Saharan Africa (not just pilots - sustained operations); (2) Geographic expansion (growing presence or retreating?); (3) Farmer base growth (acquiring new farmers or losing existing?); (4) Product roadmap (continued investment in features farmers need?); (5) Multi-year contracts (committed to farmers/partners for 3-5 years?); (6) Seasonal commitment (will platform be here for next planting season?).
questions.evidence_required: Operational history in SSA (3+ years), Geographic expansion data, Farmer acquisition/retention metrics, Product roadmap, Multi-year partnership contracts, Seasonal commitment guarantees
questions.africa_specific_notes: Many platforms pilot then exit. Farmers need multi-year commitment (crop cycles, credit history). Seasonal reliability critical - farmers plan around platform.

questions.text: Pilot-to-Scale Track Record: Demonstrate ability to scale beyond pilots: (1) Pilot history (how many pilots? outcomes?); (2) Scale-up success (how many pilots became sustained operations?); (3) Farmer retention (do farmers continue using platform after pilot ends?); (4) Geographic scale (how many countries, regions, districts?); (5) Farmer scale (how many active farmers - not just registered?); (6) Barriers to scale (what prevents scaling? how addressed?).
questions.evidence_required: Pilot documentation and outcomes, Scale-up case studies, Farmer retention data, Geographic coverage maps, Active farmer metrics, Barriers to scale analysis
questions.africa_specific_notes: Pilot-to-scale gap huge in Africa. Many pilots, few scale. Must show sustained operations, not just donor-funded pilots. Active farmers metric critical (not just registered).

questions.text: Farmer Outcome Evidence - SSA Context: Provide rigorous evidence of farmer benefits: (1) Income impact (do farmers earn more? by how much? compared to control group?); (2) Yield impact (do farmers produce more? which crops? verified data?); (3) Food security impact (do farmers have better food access?); (4) Time savings (does platform save farmer time? for what activities?); (5) Risk reduction (does platform reduce farmer risk? crop insurance, price volatility?); (6) Study quality (RCTs, quasi-experimental, or just testimonials?).
questions.evidence_required: Impact evaluation studies (RCTs preferred), Income data (treatment vs control), Yield data (verified, not self-reported), Food security assessments, Time use studies, Risk reduction analysis
questions.africa_specific_notes: Outcome evidence often weak - testimonials, not rigorous studies. Need RCTs or quasi-experimental designs. Income/yield claims must be verified, not self-reported.

questions.text: Farmer References & Testimonials: Provide verifiable farmer references: (1) Farmer testimonials (video, audio, written - in local languages); (2) Farmer contact information (can prospective farmers talk to existing users?); (3) Cooperative endorsements (do farmer organizations recommend platform?); (4) Geographic diversity (references from multiple regions, countries); (5) Farmer demographics (references from women, youth, elderly, different farm sizes); (6) Negative feedback transparency (are complaints/criticisms shared?).
questions.evidence_required: Farmer testimonial library (video, audio, local languages), Referenceable farmer list, Cooperative endorsement letters, Geographic/demographic diversity in references, Complaint/criticism transparency
questions.africa_specific_notes: Testimonials must be authentic (not paid actors). Farmer-to-farmer trust critical. Cooperative endorsements powerful. Must include negative feedback for credibility.

questions.text: Third-Party Validation & Awards: Demonstrate external recognition and validation: (1) Research institution partnerships (universities, CGIAR centers validating platform); (2) Government endorsements (Ministry of Agriculture, extension services); (3) Development partner support (World Bank, USAID, Gates Foundation); (4) Industry awards (agtech competitions, innovation prizes); (5) Media coverage (credible journalism, not just press releases); (6) Peer recognition (other agtech platforms, industry associations).
questions.evidence_required: Research partnership documentation, Government endorsement letters, Development partner grant/contract documentation, Award certifications, Media coverage archive, Industry recognition
questions.africa_specific_notes: Third-party validation important for credibility. Research institutions (local universities, CGIAR) critical. Government endorsement powerful. Awards less important than farmer outcomes.

questions.text: Farmer Pricing Fairness & Anti-Exploitation: Demonstrate fair, non-exploitative pricing: (1) Pricing transparency (all fees disclosed, no hidden charges); (2) Pricing competitiveness (vs local markets, other platforms); (3) Commission fairness (reasonable rates, not extractive); (4) Interest rate fairness (for credit - APR vs informal lenders, not predatory); (5) Pricing audits (independent verification of fairness); (6) Farmer pricing feedback (do farmers feel pricing is fair?).
questions.evidence_required: Pricing disclosure documentation, Competitive pricing analysis, Commission rate justification, Interest rate comparisons (vs market), Independent pricing audits, Farmer pricing satisfaction surveys
questions.africa_specific_notes: Farmers highly vulnerable to exploitation. Pricing must be demonstrably fair. Commission rates often extractive. Credit interest rates must not be predatory.

questions.text: Data Ethics & Farmer Data Sovereignty: Ensure ethical farmer data practices: (1) Farmer data ownership (farmers own their data, not platform); (2) Data usage consent (informed, specific, voluntary - not coerced); (3) Data benefit sharing (if data monetized, do farmers benefit?); (4) Data sovereignty (farmer data stays in Africa, not extracted to Global North); (5) Research ethics (if data used for research, farmers consented? IRB approval?); (6) Data colonialism prevention (value created from data shared with farmers).
questions.evidence_required: Data ownership policies, Consent mechanisms (farmer-friendly), Data benefit sharing agreements, Data residency policies, Research ethics approvals (IRB), Anti-data colonialism policies
questions.africa_specific_notes: Data colonialism major concern - farmer data extracted, value captured elsewhere. Farmers must own and benefit from their data. Data should stay in Africa.

questions.text: Social Impact & Community Benefit: Demonstrate positive social impact beyond profit: (1) Local employment (how many jobs created? quality of jobs?); (2) Skills development (are local staff trained for advancement?); (3) Community investment (schools, health, infrastructure - beyond platform); (4) Environmental responsibility (sustainable agriculture practices promoted?); (5) Gender equity (women farmers included? women staff hired?); (6) Youth engagement (opportunities for young farmers?).
questions.evidence_required: Local employment data, Skills development programs, Community investment documentation, Environmental impact assessments, Gender equity metrics, Youth engagement programs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Social impact beyond profit important for trust. Local job creation critical. Gender equity essential (women farmers often excluded). Environmental sustainability increasingly important.

questions.text: Climate Smart Agriculture & Carbon Integrity: For platforms promoting CSA or selling carbon credits: (1) Verification of farmer practices (satellite, ground truth, photos?); (2) Carbon credit methodology (Verra, Gold Standard?); (3) Benefit sharing (what % of carbon revenue goes to farmer?); (4) Greenwashing prevention (are claims audited?); (5) Adaptation vs Mitigation balance.
questions.evidence_required: Carbon verification reports, Benefit sharing audit, Methodology documentation
questions.africa_specific_notes: Carbon markets are growing but risky. Farmers must receive fair share of revenue. Verification must be rigorous to prevent greenwashing.

scoring_notes: Layer 5 (Integrity) for Agriculture in Sub-Saharan Africa: Financial sustainability beyond donor funding critical. Farmer outcome evidence must be rigorous (RCTs, not testimonials). Pricing fairness essential to prevent exploitation. Data sovereignty and anti-colonialism mandatory.
